summary: charape postinstall overwrites sibling Baileys packages in node_modules
details: charape's scripts/postinstall.js runs on npm install and walks up to the installer's node_modules root, then unconditionally writes package.json, index.js, and index.cjs into node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys, node_modules/@adiwajshing/baileys, and node_modules/baileys. The written stubs redirect those packages' main/exports to charape's own lib/index.cjs, so any subsequent require('@whiskeysockets/baileys') (or the two aliases) in the same project loads charape's code instead of the Baileys package the installer declared. No existence check guards the writes, so pre-existing real Baileys installations at those paths are clobbered. The same postinstall additionally writes legacy-peer-deps=true into the installer's project.npmrc, weakening future dependency resolution without consent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
